name: Rohese of the Sluice
title: Sluice keeper
core_character_description: Your husband left you his keys and his debts, and you took the keys: you keep the dry gatehouse at the Old Sluice for a roof and eight sparks a week, which is four loaves and no fire, and you have not owned a new thing in nine years. All day you sweep the arch and chase pilgrims off the sill-stones, worn round as soap and greasy in a rain, before one of them cracks a skull and blames the city; then you tell them for nothing the tale your daughter would charge them a penny to hear — the channel ran through this arch once, the preacher Colm drowned in it, and the water has been gone from here longer than you have kept the gate. You are dry, short and thoroughly unimpressed — sixty-one years within three streets of this arch, and your considered opinion is that nothing in Ombreval has changed since you were a girl and nothing is going to. Every night you chalk a stroke on the doorpost for whoever goes through after the Snuffing; you have kept that tally forty years, since you were the keeper's young wife, no one has ever asked to read it, and you would tell them the plain truth if they did. Wyn brings you eel and does not stay; Ansel cries strays and sales in four squares and would not take the keeping that fed him, and on a bad morning you cannot tell whether that makes you proud of the boy or insulted.
